title: Revert v47.8 --ipv4/--ipv6-timeout options (crash regression)
description:
Build 144 on TestFlight crashed for the PO on the first channel selection with EXC_BAD_ACCESS / SIGSEGV at libvlc_media_player_new (offset 16, x0=NULL). Crash incident C05C70B4-769E-492F-80B2-F3CFCFDEAF77 on 2026-05-21 07:57:05.

Root cause: the --ipv4-timeout=2000 and --ipv6-timeout=2000 libvlc options I added in v47.8 are not recognized by this MobileVLCKit's bundled libvlc. When VLCMediaPlayer(options:) is constructed with them, libvlc fails to initialize its instance, VLCLibrary's internal p_libvlc_int ends up NULL, and the subsequent libvlc_media_player_new call dereferences NULL and segfaults.

The first VLCMediaPlayer() at AudioPlayerService init() didn't crash because it uses no options (default-config libvlc). Crash happens on the first retirePlayer(options:) call — i.e., the first channel play attempt.

Fix: remove --ipv4-timeout and --ipv6-timeout from both retirePlayer(options:) call sites (startStream and the buffered-playback path). Replace v47.8's option-block comment with a warning that documents these options crashed and should not be re-added without verifying the libvlc version supports them.

This was the exact failure mode the 2026-05-20-18 retro warned about: shipped a defensive change without validating that the libvlc option names were valid for this build. The bd v47.8 close note literally said 'exact knob varies by MobileVLCKit version' — should have verified before shipping.
close_reason: Removed --ipv4-timeout=2000 and --ipv6-timeout=2000 from both retirePlayer(options:) call sites in AudioPlayerService.swift (startStream around line 750, buffered-playback around line 1010). Left a code-comment warning at the startStream site documenting that these options crash libvlc init in this MobileVLCKit version and should not be re-added without verification. Build 145 succeeded; app launches and 52 unit tests pass.

title: OIDC sign-in returns HTTP 500 from app (works in web browser)
description: After the discovery/URL-first fix (1e4), the SSO button appears and opens Google auth, but completing 'Login with Google' returns HTTP 500 from the ABS server. The SAME OIDC login works fine in a standard web browser to the same install (bookshelf.endofline.tech, ABS 2.35.1) — so it's specific to our MOBILE OIDC flow (GET /auth/openid with client-PKCE + redirect_uri=adagiostream://oauth, then GET /auth/openid/callback with code_verifier), not the server's web flow. The 500 is server-side; the app is likely sending something the mobile path rejects (candidate causes: client_id value 'AdagioStream' vs what ABS expects, code_verifier/code_challenge PKCE handling in the mobile exchange, the shared-cookie/session between /auth/openid and /auth/openid/callback not carrying across the ASWebAuthenticationSession boundary, or a redirect_uri exact-match issue). Need: the ABS server log for the 500, and a primary-source comparison of our flow vs the official audiobookshelf-app mobile OIDC implementation + ABS server openid callback source.
notes: Build 196: attach captured /auth/openid cookies (connect.sid, auth_method) as an explicit Cookie: header on /auth/openid/callback. Build 195 captured the session cookie but the manual HTTPCookieStorage() returned [] via cookies(for:) ('will send cookies: []') -> 400 No session; 196 bypasses the storage entirely. Verified iOS build + 594 tests + tvOS all green (synchronous cookieHeader test, no async). Merged+pushed 196. AWAITING user SSO test on 196 — look for '[OIDC] callback attaching cookies: [connect.sid,auth_method]' + success. If STILL No session with the Cookie header attached -> server-side (ABS in-memory session lost between requests / Pangolin stripping the inbound Cookie header). Follow-ups after SSO confirmed: strip all TEMP-OIDC-DEBUG logging.
close_reason: FIXED + reporter-confirmed on build 196 (SSO/Google login completes). Root causes fixed across builds 192-196: (192) percent-encode + in the auth code; (194) read /auth/openid Location header instead of following the 302; (195) capture ABS's /auth/openid Set-Cookie; (196) attach the captured connect.sid as an explicit Cookie header on /auth/openid/callback (the manual HTTPCookieStorage() wouldn't return cookies via cookies(for:)). title: ABS concurrent 401s double-rotate refresh token -> forced re-login
description: CONFIRMED HIGH. AudiobookshelfAuth.authorizedData (~:158-181) + refresh (~:191-225). Actor isolation does NOT serialize across await suspension. Two concurrent authed requests near token expiry both read the stale access token, both 401, both call refresh(). Refresh #1 rotates R1->R2 and persists; refresh #2 POSTs the now-invalid R1 -> rejected -> forgetTokens() clears the freshly-rotated pair -> next request forces a full username/password re-login. The Books tab fires loadBooks + coverURL + itemsInProgress concurrently, so this triggers in practice. Fix: coalesce refreshes (single inFlightRefresh Task others await), or skip refresh if tokens.accessToken already changed since the 401. Add a two-concurrent-401 test (untested path).

title: ABS reverse-proxy subpath deployments broken (buildURL drops host path)
description: CONFIRMED HIGH. AudiobookshelfAPI.swift buildURL (~:275-285) uses URL(string: "/api/...", relativeTo: host); an absolute-path reference replaces the host's entire path, so host https://abs.example.com/audiobookshelf + /api/libraries resolves to https://abs.example.com/api/libraries — the /audiobookshelf subpath is DROPPED. Fix: preserve host.path (build URLComponents from host, set path = host.path + path), or require leading-slash-free paths with a trailing-slash host. Add a subpath-host buildURL unit test (none exists).

title: Library-track resume: audible blip of track start before seek lands
description:
Follow-up reported on GitHub issue #3 (build 247) after the beads_mobilemusic-9nf fix landed: the last-radio-station bug is gone, but resuming a paused library track now audibly plays a split second from the beginning of the track before jumping to the paused position.

Root cause: AudioPlayerService.reactivateAndPlayLibraryTrack(...) (Services/AudioPlayerService.swift ~line 1035) calls startLibraryTrack(...) which starts VLC playback from position 0 immediately, then seeks to the saved elapsed position only after a heuristic 1-second delay (VLC needs the media parsed before mediaPlayer.time is honoured — see existing comment at that call site). Real audio therefore flows from position 0 for up to ~1s before the seek lands, which the listener hears as a blip of the track intro.
acceptance_criteria: Resuming a paused library track (via lock-screen Play, or any path through reactivateAndPlayLibraryTrack with a non-zero seekTo) does not audibly play any audio from the track's start before landing on the paused position — the user only hears audio starting at (approximately) the position where they paused.
notes: Fix implemented: AudioOutput.swift adds setMuted(_:) (mainMixerNode.outputVolume = 0/1). AudioPlayerService.reactivateAndPlayLibraryTrack mutes before starting playback whenever a non-zero seekTo is given, flushes the VLC ring buffer (VLCAudioCallbackBridge.flushBuffer()) right when the seek is applied to drop any pre-seek samples, and unmutes 0.2s after the seek to let the buffer refill from the new position. Bounded/self-healing: unmute always fires from the same delayed block regardless of startLibraryTrack success, so mute can't get stuck longer than ~1.2s. Compiles clean (iOS + tvOS). Could not runtime-verify: simulator unavailable locally (pre-existing CoreSimulator/Xcode mismatch). Needs on-device verification: pause a library track, resume via lock screen, confirm no audible blip of the track intro before it lands on the paused position.
close_reason: Implemented and compile-verified (iOS + tvOS); runtime verification pending due to local simulator being unavailable

title: Lock-screen resume plays last radio station instead of resuming paused library track
description:
Reported as GitHub issue #3 (App 1.2 build 243, iPhone 14 Pro, iOS 26.5). Repro: play a library track, lock the screen, pause via lock-screen controls, then resume via lock-screen controls — it plays the last-listened Live radio station instead of resuming the track.

Root cause: AudioPlayerService.resume() (Services/AudioPlayerService.swift ~line 2671) is radio-only — it unconditionally does 'guard let channel = currentChannel ?? lastPlayedChannel else { return }; play(channel: channel)'. When a library track is playing, currentChannel is nil (cleared at library-track start, see comment at line ~1902 'Transition state: track mode sets currentChannel to nil'), so resume() falls through to lastPlayedChannel — whatever radio station was last played before switching to library — and starts that instead. pause() does NOT clear currentTrack/playbackSource, so the paused library state (playbackSource == .library(queue:, index:), queueAPI, trackElapsed) is still available at resume time; resume() just never checks it.

MPRemoteCommandCenter's playCommand target (configureRemoteCommands, ~line 3485) calls resume() directly, so this hits both the lock screen and any other remote-command play control (CarPlay, headphones, etc.), not just the lock screen.
acceptance_criteria: Play a library track, pause via a remote command (lock screen Play/Pause, or togglePlayPauseCommand), then resume via a remote command: the same track resumes from approximately where it was paused (not restarted from 0, not the last radio station). Existing radio pause/resume behavior (play(channel:) via currentChannel/lastPlayedChannel) is unchanged.
notes: Fix implemented in AudioPlayerService.resume() (Services/AudioPlayerService.swift): checks playbackSource for .library(queue:, index:) before falling back to the radio-only currentChannel/lastPlayedChannel path, and resumes via reactivateAndPlayLibraryTrack(...) with seekTo: trackElapsed (trackElapsed survives pause() — only stop() and track-start reset it to 0). Compiles clean (iOS + tvOS). No existing unit test coverage for resume() found in AdagioStreamTests. Could not runtime-verify: this Mac's CoreSimulator is out of date vs the installed Xcode, blocking all simulator builds/tests locally (pre-existing env issue, unrelated to this fix). Needs manual verification (play a library track, lock screen, pause/resume via lock-screen controls) once that's resolved.

title: Screen doesn't auto-lock during music/radio playback (VLCKit idle-timer leak)
description: VLCKit's MobileVLCKit.framework binary calls setIdleTimerDisabled: on UIApplication internally (confirmed via strings on the binary), and does not reliably restore it, especially for audio-only playback where no video drawable is ever attached (AudioOutput routes VLC audio via an amem callback into AVAudioEngine — no drawable set). AudioPlayerService's single shared VLCMediaPlayer instance backs both radio and library playback, so the bug affects both. Symptom: while AdagioStream is in the foreground playing music or radio, the screen never auto-locks per the system Auto-Lock setting; switching to another app restores normal auto-lock behavior. Fix: force UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled = false centrally (e.g. in the mediaPlayerStateChanged VLCMediaPlayerDelegate callback in AudioPlayerService.swift) to override VLCKit's internal management, since this app has no legitimate video-playback reason to ever disable the idle timer.
acceptance_criteria: Playing music or radio in the foreground, the screen auto-locks per system Auto-Lock timeout, same as when the app is not playing anything.
notes: Fix implemented in AudioPlayerService.swift mediaPlayerStateChanged: force UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled = false on every VLC state transition, on iOS only. Root cause confirmed via strings on MobileVLCKit.framework binary — it calls setIdleTimerDisabled: internally. Compiles clean (iOS + tvOS). Could not runtime-verify on-device/simulator: this Mac's CoreSimulator (1051.54.0) is out of date vs the installed Xcode, blocking all simulator builds locally (pre-existing env issue, unrelated to this fix). Needs manual verification once that's resolved.

title: Music tab: artist list spinner never resolves (ObservableObject not observed)
description:
On the phone Music tab, the Artists view shows a perpetual 'Loading artists…' spinner. Switching the browse-mode segmented control to Albums (which loads fine) and back to Artists makes the artist list appear — confirming the data loaded but the view didn't re-render.

Root cause: MusicLibraryView stores the view model as a plain @State (MusicLibraryView.swift:49 — @State private var viewModel: NavidromeLibraryViewModel?). @State does not subscribe to an ObservableObject's @Published changes, so when loadArtists() transitions artistsState .loading→.loaded, MusicLibraryView's body never recomputes. The artist list is rendered inline via the artistBrowser(vm:api:) method (MusicLibraryView.swift:247-303), so it depends on MusicLibraryView's own (absent) observation.

Why other tabs work: BrowseAlbumsView/GenreListView/PlaylistListView/ArtistDetailView are separate views declaring @ObservedObject var viewModel, so they observe correctly. Switching browseMode mutates a real @State (browseMode), forcing a body recompute that re-reads the now-.loaded artistsState — the 'fix' the user stumbled into.

Fix: extract the artist browser into its own ArtistBrowserView with @ObservedObject var viewModel, mirroring the sibling browse views.

Refs:
- MusicLibraryView.swift:49 — @State viewModel (not observed)
- MusicLibraryView.swift:247-303 — inlined artistBrowser switch
- NavidromeLibraryViewModel.swift:17-23 — @MainActor ObservableObject, @Published artistsState
close_reason: Extracted artist list into standalone ArtistBrowserView with @ObservedObject view model so it re-renders on artistsState changes; mirrors sibling browse views. Build 170 succeeds, app launches.

title: Siri/interruption: audio leaks for a couple seconds during interruption (AudioOutput restarts engine while interrupted)
description: FIELD BUG (user-reported, CarPlay + SiriusXM radio, ~/adagiostream-debug.log). On an AVAudioSession interruption (Siri reading a text), the app 'rides out' the interruption keeping VLC running, so AudioOutput.intendedToRun stays true. Siri/CarPlay fire a route/format change; AudioOutput's config-change handler (AudioOutput.swift ~line 127 'engine configuration changed (route/format) — restarting engine') restarts the AVAudioEngine WHILE the interruption is active -> ~2s of audible playback over Siri, then stop. Contrast: when idle it correctly logs 'configuration changed while idle — not restarting (intendedToRun=false)' (~line 124). Reproduces across multiple Siri windows in the log (17:27:50, 18:09:23). FIX: AudioOutput must not (re)start the engine while an AVAudioSession interruption is in effect — gate restart on (intendedToRun && !isInterrupted). AudioPlayerService should inform AudioOutput of interruption began/ended (began at AudioPlayerService:395, ended at :448, ride-out at :409). VLC ride-out buffering may continue; engine OUTPUT must stay suspended until interruption ends. Affects radio + Navidrome music (shared path). Field validation required (can't repro Siri in sim) — keep the AudioOutput:124/127 diagnostic logs so the next drive shows 'not restarting — interrupted' instead of 'restarting engine'.
notes: Field verification consolidated into the single drive checklist (see 'CarPlay field-validation drive' task created 2026-07-08). Fix committed 5bdf2ee build 169; expect 'configuration changed while interrupted — not restarting' during Siri windows.
close_reason: FIELD CONFIRMED by PO on drive (2026-07-08): no audio bleed during Siri interruption; fix 5bdf2ee validated

title: CarPlay: music resumed during Siri-initiated phone call — instrument resume decision (China-safe, no CallKit)
description:
On 2026-06-11 ~08:19 on CarPlay, playing 'Radio: Alt2K', the user made a phone call via Siri and music resumed while the call was still active.

VERIFIED FROM LOG (adagiostream-debug.log):
- Two interruption .began (08:19:08.342, 08:19:11.435), single .ended (08:19:15.151) with shouldResume=true, ridingOut=true.
- App rode out the interruption and resumed VLC from cache at 08:19:15 ('VLC survived interruption — seamless resume', AudioPlayerService.swift:464).
- No further interruption events until CarPlay physically disconnected at 08:20:53 (oldDeviceUnavailable, user left car) ~98s later.
- At 08:19:15.693 the app's setActive(true) SUCCEEDED ('short interruption: session active, otherWasPlaying=false') — mild counter-evidence that the session was free at that instant.

NOT CONFIRMED (gap):
- Whether a phone call was actually active at the moment of resume. The log contains NO call-state signal. The two-.began/one-.ended asymmetry is suggestive (a second interruption may never have sent .ended) but could also be iOS re-posting .began on the routeConfigurationChange at 08:19:08.449. Cannot distinguish from this log.
- The 'Siri->call handoff' theory is a HYPOTHESIS, not verified against a primary source.

CONSTRAINT: App ships on China App Store. CallKit (incl. CXCallObserver) is an App Store risk in China (MIIT regulation; Apple has pulled apps that use CallKit even just to pause audio for incoming calls). So the diagnostic must NOT link CallKit, and we are NOT region-gating it for a mere diagnostic.

PLAN (instrumentation only, NO behavior change):
At .ended decision point (AudioPlayerService.swift:418), log: shouldResume, isOtherAudioPlaying, secondaryAudioShouldBeSilenced, and a running began/ended pair count. Then poll the session for a few seconds AFTER resume (log isOtherAudioPlaying + route) to capture the case where a call takes audio back after we reactivate — the window this log never showed.

Caveat: isOtherAudioPlaying may not reflect a system phone call; if it comes back clean we will have ruled it out and know we need a different signal. Resume behavior unchanged until a log shows what owns audio at and just after resume.
notes: Field verification consolidated into drive checklist beads_mobilemusic-q0x (2026-07-08). On next drive: incoming call while playing must NOT resume music over the call; check call-aware resume-decision instrumentation.

2. If absent, identify alternatives:

     #if TARGET_OS_TV

title: Phase: Replace VLCKit audio output with app-owned AVAudioEngine pipeline
description:
Root-cause fix for the Apple Music focus grab. VLCKit's iOS audiounit module owns the AVAudioSession and calls setActive(false, .notifyOthersOnDeactivation) on mediaPlayer.stop() (confirmed via VLC 3.0.x source). Workarounds (assertSessionOwnership pre-debounce in build 146) don't prevent it because the deactivation is hardcoded with no opt-out flag.

Real fix: register PCM callbacks via libvlc_audio_set_callbacks(), which switches VLC to in-memory output (amem module). audiounit_ios is never loaded; SessionManager is never invoked; no setActive(false) on stop. AdagioStream owns AVAudioSession exclusively and routes PCM through its own AVAudioEngine.

Requires reaching into VLCKit private API (VLCMediaPlayer+Internal.h playerInstance) via a thin Objective-C bridge in the AdagioStream target, since the framework modulemap excludes the libvlc C headers.

Children:
1. ObjC bridge + spike — prove amem callbacks prevent VLC session manipulation
2. PCM pipeline — AVAudioEngine routing, format negotiation, threading
3. Session ownership + integration — Adagio owns AVAudioSession; rewire interruption / route / NowPlaying / CarPlay paths
4. Cleanup — remove the assertSessionOwnership workarounds layered in earlier

description:
Companion to mobilemusic-7rr. ProviderManager.updateProvider() replaces the provider in-place and calls saveProviders() unconditionally; if the user edits a working provider to broken credentials, the broken state is persisted before loadChannels() reveals the failure.

Fix: pre-validate the updated provider with loadChannelsWithRetry before replacement. If it throws or returns 0 channels, set error and return without modifying providers — the prior good config stays intact on disk. Only on successful validation do we replace + save + refresh.

Call site is AddProviderView.swift lines 163-174 (editing branch).

title: Reject failing playlist adds — don't persist providers with 0 channels

title: Fix Apple Music focus grab during channel change
description:
When Apple Music is playing, user opens Adagio and plays a stream (works fine), then changes channels — during the 1.5s debounce window in AudioPlayerService.play(), Apple Music auto-resumes briefly because mediaPlayer.stop() runs immediately but the session-takeover dance (setActive(false, .notifyOthersOnDeactivation) → setActive(true)) is deferred until startStream() runs after the debounce.

Root cause: AudioPlayerService.swift:604 calls mediaPlayer.stop() immediately, but the session takeover at lines 709-712 lives inside startStream(), which is debounced 1.5s when needsDelay is true.

Fix: move the session-takeover dance into play() itself, before the debounce timer is scheduled, so Adagio asserts session ownership before yielding the 1.5s window.

Instrumentation: log isOtherAudioPlaying values at three points — entry to play(), just after mediaPlayer.stop(), and just before startStream() runs — so we can confirm Apple Music sneaks in during the gap if the fix doesn't fully resolve it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bound VLC network read so poll() can't hang on stalled sockets
description:
Root cause of the watchdog kill is Thread 11 in vlc_tls_Read → vlc_poll_i11e_inner → poll() on a TLS socket that stopped delivering bytes (cell radio stalled during incoming call). poll() had no short timeout, so VLC's input thread sat indefinitely and starved every join up the chain.

Investigate MobileVLCKit options to bound this. Candidates (exact names vary by VLCKit version):
- :http-reconnect (already set per debug log)
- :network-caching=10000 (already set; controls buffer not socket timeout)
- :ipv4-timeout / :ipv6-timeout — connection-time timeouts
- :sout-livehttp-caching — output side, not input
- Lower-level: configure custom VLCMedia options to add :clock-jitter and a tighter input timeout
- Worst case: post-process by adding a watchdog that calls media = nil if no bytes flow for N seconds

Reference the existing zero-byte retry logic (vlcZeroByteRetryCount, line 588) and the Buffering timeout retry at line ~1372 — there's already a 20s no-data timeout but it only fires DURING playback startup, not for an established stream that stalls.

Acceptance: a stalled HLS socket triggers media=nil within ≤2s, freeing VLC's input thread before any teardown is attempted.
close_reason:
Added --ipv4-timeout=2000 and --ipv6-timeout=2000 to both retirePlayer call sites (startStream and the buffered-playback path).

Research findings (recorded inline in startStream): VLC's steady-state poll() inside vlc_tls_Read uses an infinite timeout that cannot be configured via libvlc options. The connect timeouts only bound the initial TCP handshake (defaults to 5s, now 2s). For mid-stream stalls — the actual crash mechanism — the syncState() data-flow watchdog (dataFlowStaleTimeout = 8s, line 75) is the only mechanism, and it already exists.

So v47.8 ships a narrow improvement (faster reconnect on connection-time stalls) and documents the unfixable steady-state case. The combined v47 fix surface is:
- v47.5: timing instrumentation on all 8 VLC teardown call sites
- v47.6: detach media before stop in retirePlayer (input severed before drain)
- v47.7: closure capture audit complete — orphan reference lives inside VLCKit
- v47.8: 2s connect timeouts + documented limit

Build 141 succeeded; 52 unit tests pass.

title: Audit closure captures for orphan VLCMediaPlayer strong references
description:
Find the second strong reference to VLCMediaPlayer that escaped retirePlayer's [old] utility-queue release pattern. Stack trace shows _Block_release on a main-queue block triggered the dealloc, meaning some block on main was holding a reference that outlived the [old] capture.

Audit targets in AudioPlayerService.swift:
1. interruptionFallbackWorkItem (line 288) — DispatchWorkItem retained by asyncAfter, captures self
2. channelNameOverlayWorkItem (line 600) — DispatchWorkItem captures [weak self]
3. The 0.5s post-interruption closure (line 339) — no [weak self], captures self strongly
4. Any other DispatchWorkItem/asyncAfter that touches self.mediaPlayer
5. VLC delegate callbacks — verify VLCKit's delegate is assign/unsafe_unretained (should be) and not retaining the player back
6. Any local 'let p = mediaPlayer' patterns that escape into closures

Grep starting point:
    grep -nE 'mediaPlayer|VLCMediaPlayer' AdagioStream/Services/AudioPlayerService.swift | grep -v '^\s*//'

If a real orphan is found, either capture [weak self] or convert to a dedicated [weak mediaPlayer] capture and guard.
close_reason:
Audit complete. NO orphan VLCMediaPlayer reference found in app code:

1. retirePlayer's [old] capture is the only explicit player capture; dispatched to utility queue.
2. All DispatchWorkItem closures (interruptionFallbackWorkItem line 320, channelNameOverlayWorkItem line 632, debounce workItem line 651) use [weak self].
3. The two interruption.ended asyncAfter closures (lines 371, 408) strong-capture self but access self.mediaPlayer (re-evaluated per call) — so they reach the NEW player after a retirePlayer, not the OLD one.
4. Combine sinks (sxmCancellable line 179, espnCancellable line 190) use [weak self].
5. VLC delegate methods are 'nonisolated' wrappers that dispatch Task { @MainActor in } — no aNotification capture, and self is either weakly captured or accessed via self.mediaPlayer.
6. NotificationCenter observers all target AVAudioSession.sharedInstance(), not the media player.

Conclusion: the orphan reference responsible for the dealloc-on-main in the FRONTBOARD crash most likely lives inside VLCKit's own dispatch internals (VLCKit posts state-change notifications via NSNotification with the player as object; the runloop's pending notification queue can strong-retain the player). That's outside our control.

The right mitigation is v47.6 (detach media before stop, done) + v47.8 (bound the network read so poll() can't hang regardless of who runs the final dealloc).

title: Detach media before stop in retirePlayer (safer teardown order)
description:
In AudioPlayerService.swift retirePlayer() (line 119), the current order is:
    old.stop()       // line 121
    old.media = nil  // line 122
    old.delegate = nil  // line 123

Swap so media is detached BEFORE stop is called:
    old.media = nil  // sever the input source first
    old.delegate = nil
    old.stop()       // now has nothing to drain

Rationale: stop() can synchronously join VLC's input/decoder threads. If the input thread is in vlc_stream_ReadPartial → poll() on a stalled socket, stop() inherits the block. Clearing media first signals the input layer to exit before stop runs.

Low-risk change. Pair with the instrumentation issue to verify the new ordering doesn't introduce a different stall.
close_reason: Swapped order in retirePlayer to detach media (and clear delegate) BEFORE calling stop(). stop() synchronously drains VLC's input/decoder threads, so clearing media first severs the input source. Build 141; 52 tests pass.

description:

b) Targets were registered to the wrong AudioPlayerService instance (singleton drift?)
c) The remote events were arriving but ignored because some 'ready' guard wasn't satisfied yet
d) iOS itself wasn't routing remote events to the app until something else happened around 16:51:46

Investigate:

2. Add a log line at the moment each target is registered (and confirm it ran).
3. Add a log when a remote command is RECEIVED but rejected by any guard (the current REMOTE logs only fire on accepted commands).

What it does:
1. Logs current audio session category/mode/route, current MPNowPlayingInfoCenter state, and playbackState at CarPlay connect — so the next incident log shows what iOS thinks of us before user action.
2. If nowPlayingInfo is nil, writes a placeholder (rate=0, isLiveStream=true) and sets playbackState=.stopped. The placeholder declares us as a now-playing candidate so iOS routes MPRemoteCommandCenter events to us BEFORE the user picks a channel. Doesn't stomp an active playback session (guards on existingInfo == nil).
3. Re-asserts session.setActive(true) so any stale post-interruption state is cleared.

If providers is still empty at that moment (e.g. Keychain or persistence is slow on a cold launch), enabled is empty, missing is empty, and the function exits with 'all enabled providers loaded — no retry needed' even though nothing has loaded.

- OR: kick the recovery off providerManager.$providers (combine with $channels) so it only counts as 'loaded' once we have BOTH a non-empty providers list AND non-zero counts per provider.

- The 'all loaded' log path requires at least one enabled provider in providers, not just empty == empty.

title: Add NWPathMonitor-driven player reconnect on Wi-Fi <-> cellular path transitions
description:
Currently AudioPlayerService has no network-path monitoring (grep NWPathMonitor returns nothing). VLC's built-in http-reconnect handles connection drops but not network interface changes — when a user walks out of Wi-Fi range onto cellular (or vice versa), the player can stall and not recover.

Implementation sketch:
- Add NWPathMonitor in AudioPlayerService, start on init, stop on deinit
- On path transition (status .satisfied after .unsatisfied, OR isExpensive flips, OR primary interface changes), if currentChannel is set and player state is .error/.stopped/.buffering > N seconds, trigger a fresh player rebuild + retune of the current channel
- Reuse the existing retirePlayer(options:) + startStream() flow so we don't duplicate the tear-down logic
- Log path transitions to the .player category

Avoid: reacting to every transient path event (debounce/cooldown so we don't thrash); reconnecting when playback is healthy
close_reason: Added NWPathMonitor in AudioPlayerService. Init-time monitor logs initial path state; subsequent updates trigger a player rebuild via play(channel:) when status flips unsatisfied->satisfied or the primary interface changes (Wi-Fi <-> cellular). 5s cooldown debounces rapid handoffs. play(channel:)'s same-channel guard is bypassed by clearing isActiveSession first. Build green, 52/52 tests pass, simulator launches. Real-world verification requires enabling Diagnostics logging and toggling airplane mode / Wi-Fi off during playback.

title: Add http-reconnect / http-continuous / audio-time-stretch VLC instance options for cellular resilience
description:
Add three libvlc options at instance creation in AudioPlayerService.startStream():
- --http-reconnect: auto-reconnect on HTTP-level drops
- --http-continuous: continue reading on transient HTTP errors instead of failing the playback
- --audio-time-stretch: allow ±2% rate adjustment to recover from buffer drift instead of dropping samples

Must be set at VLCMediaPlayer init time (alongside --network-caching), NOT via media.addOptions — libvlc rejects those as unsafe via libvlc_media_add_option (see comment at AudioPlayerService.swift:599-601). Only applies to the live-stream path (line ~605); the buffered-file playback path at line ~803 plays a local file and does not need HTTP options.

title: Spike: gapless playback (double-buffered 2nd VLC instance vs amem pipeline)
description:
Spike complete. Decision: DEFER.

KEY FINDINGS (from reading VLCAudioCallbackBridge.m, AudioOutput.swift, AudioPlayerService.swift):

1. GLOBAL SINGLETON RING BUFFER — adg_ring_buffer/head/tail are static globals in VLCAudioCallbackBridge.m. A second VLCMediaPlayer with amem callbacks would write into the SAME ring as the first. Two decoders would race, producing interleaved garbage. Double-buffering requires refactoring the bridge from global singleton to per-player ring.

2. RENDER BLOCK ATTACHED ONCE — AVAudioSourceNode render closure is captured permanently at AudioOutput.init. It always calls pullFramesIntoLeft:right: on the global ring. Switching which buffer it drains at runtime requires an _Atomic pointer indirection in the bridge or a full node detach/reattach (which causes an engine restart gap worse than the current gap).

3. retirePlayer BACKGROUND-DISPOSE IS LOAD-BEARING — The comment in retirePlayer explicitly documents that skipping pthread_join background-dispose caused 0x8BADF00D watchdog kills. Media-swap-in-place (without retire) shares this exact risk. Not a safe shortcut.

4. GAP COMPOSITION — Most of the gap is in old.stop() (VLC drain) + decode startup latency (~50-150ms for local files). The double-buffer approach pre-warming the next track could close this, but only if the second player reaches the first play_cb before ring A empties.

5. CLEAN PATH EXISTS but requires 4 steps: (a) per-player AdgRing struct in bridge, (b) A/B ring slot + atomic switch in AudioOutput, (c) GaplessPrewarmController in AudioPlayerService, (d) edge-case wiring for skip/seek/interruption during pre-warm. This is a multi-file architectural change to the most delicate subsystem.

Design document written to docs/adr/0004-gapless-playback-design-and-deferral.md with full step-by-step implementation plan for a future session.
close_reason: Full implementation-ready gapless design delivered: docs/design/gapless-playback.md (current vs target architecture w/ file:line + per-thread analysis, per-player ring via libvlc opaque ptr, AudioOutput A/B atomic crossover, GaplessPrewarmController, full edge-case state machine, real-time-safety rules, session-safety argument, feature flag + transparent fallback, 3-phase rollout, test plan, risks, 6 PO open questions).
